purpose: AI-loadable reasoning primitives for design engineering. No visual reference collection or page-type presets.
retrieval_guidance: Select by unresolved question; read only relevant full cards. Keyword scores are hints, not a substitute for reasoning.

records.name: problem-coevolution
records.title: Problem framing as iterative hypothesis
signals: The given solution shape (a page, dashboard, form) may not fully express the underlying user problem.

records.name: divergent-exploration
records.title: Explore meaningful alternatives before converging
signals: A substantial design brief admits distinct plausible interpretations or compositions.

records.name: fixation
records.title: Detect and escape design fixation
signals: First idea, existing examples or an initial style selection are narrowing exploration.

records.name: intent-and-context
records.title: Design for actual intent, not interface labels
signals: A requested interface contains multiple actions, user expertise levels or consequences.

records.name: perceptual-grouping
records.title: Express information relationships through grouping
signals: Elements appear related but the meaning is unclear, or unrelated content appears as a single group.

records.name: information-scent
records.title: Make paths and destinations predictable
signals: Users must select among navigation routes, filters, search results or destination links.

records.name: compositional-judgment
records.title: Balance rhythm, proportion, unity and tension intentionally
signals: A screen is functional but unconvincing, flat, misweighted or visually overworked.

records.name: multidimensional-aesthetics
records.title: Evaluate perceived aesthetics as multiple dimensions
signals: A design seems polished but ordinary, or striking but difficult to understand.

records.name: novelty-and-recognition
records.title: Balance new expression with recognizable meaning
signals: A design brief wants distinctive identity without sacrificing comprehension.

records.name: visual-attention
records.title: Allocate attention without inventing eye tracking
signals: Important content is not noticed or decorative motion competes with meaning.

records.name: consistency-and-feedback
records.title: Use consistency for predictability, not uniformity
signals: Multiple actions or states are similar, inconsistent, hidden, destructive or confusing.

records.name: choice-and-targets
records.title: Design understandable choices and physically operable targets
signals: Users must choose among alternatives or operate small/close controls.

records.name: accessibility-and-craft
records.title: Treat clarity, accessibility and implementation craft as distinct requirements
signals: A visual concept is ready for implementation or release.

records.name: evaluation-validity
records.title: Evaluate appeal, usefulness and performance separately
signals: An A/B test or design review risks turning model judgment into apparent objective proof.

records.name: validation-loops
records.title: Prototype and inspect in the actual medium
signals: Source code looks plausible but visual/interaction reality is uncertain.

records.name: identity-and-meaning
records.title: Build coherent identity from meaning, not visual repetition
signals: A visual system needs memorability but cannot depend only on a signature illustration or color.

records.name: semantics-and-syntax
records.title: Clarify meaning, internal language and pragmatic use
signals: Ask three different questions: what does it mean, what makes the language coherent, and does it work for its audience?

records.name: usefulness-and-honesty
records.title: Make the artifact understandable, useful and honest
signals: Challenge every feature and visual cue to explain what it enables or clarifies.

records.name: brief-questioning
records.title: Interrogate assumptions before committing to form
signals: Ask what the stated brief might be missing and what matters to users or the organization.

records.name: delayed-commitment
records.title: Keep exploratory uncertainty alive just long enough
signals: Resist prematurely declaring the first coherent design the best design.

records.name: metaphor-legibility
records.title: Test competing visual metaphors at use size
signals: Different symbols may encode the same function with different recognition costs.

records.name: medium-feedback
records.title: Prototype within the medium and shorten feedback loops
signals: A static comp may hide what happens in actual interaction or responsive environments.

records.name: human-centered-exploration
records.title: Move between user learning, divergent possibilities and prototypes
signals: Treat a design process as flexible inquiry rather than a fixed sequence of workshops.

records.name: aesthetic-constructs
records.title: Distinguish what visual attractiveness actually means
signals: A visually tidy UI may still lack identity; a visually bold page may still be incoherent.
records.review: publisher/institution abstract or official normative text; no full-text guarantee

records.name: first-impressions
records.title: Separate very-early visual impressions from durable task value
signals: An unusual interface may be judged differently at first glance than after sustained use.
records.review: publisher/institution abstract or official normative text; no full-text guarantee

records.name: quantitative-perception
records.title: Choose quantitative encodings based on decoding tasks
signals: A dashboard needs accurate comparison of several quantities.
records.review: publisher/institution abstract or official normative text; no full-text guarantee

records.name: nested-validation
records.title: Validate the correct layer of a visualization design

records.title: Investigate unfamiliar domains before codifying UI patterns

records.name: content-layout-codesign

signals: Generic cards squeeze different content roles into an identical layout.
A comparison table and a process flow need different visual structure despite sharing a section.
